posts.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
posts.summary: Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs. What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs…
bullets: AI inference generates massive amounts of back-end data, such as logs and cached context, which can be 130 times larger than the actual output file.
McKinsey projects AI inference demand will grow at a 35% CAGR through 2030, outpacing training demand and consuming over 40% of data center capacity.
Inadequate storage planning risks expensive GPU idle time, as accelerators often wait for data to be retrieved from storage systems.

posts.title: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
posts.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores. Those advances have…
bullets: Enterprise AI success is shifting from model selection to the engineering of the 'serving harness,' which manages memory, scheduling, and architecture.
Technical executives must prioritize workload-specific constraints—such as latency and GPU utilization—over raw model capability to ensure production reliability.
A model that offers marginal accuracy gains may be a poor business choice if it significantly increases inference costs or fails to meet operational performance requirements.

posts.title: Making the case for context-aware AI
posts.summary: Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships that determine whether a decision is the right one. As companies look to move AI from experimentation into everyday operations, the challenge ahead…
bullets: AI agents require deep integration with operational data and business processes to avoid costly mistakes and inefficient resource consumption.
Decision intelligence relies on a contextual layer that allows agents to operate within defined guardrails and understand the specific business conditions of a task.
Organizations should focus on automating high-value, complex decision steps rather than simple tasks to maximize the ROI of AI deployments.

posts.title: Chip Scaling Moves Beyond The Transistor
posts.summary:
SEMICON West 2026: Advanced packaging, photonics, test, and AI are increasingly intertwined; very different conversations ahead. 
The post Chip Scaling Moves Beyond The Transistor appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The semiconductor industry is projected to reach a $2 trillion market valuation by 2030, with 300mm fab equipment spending expected to hit $227 billion by 2029.
Scaling is no longer just about transistor density; it has become a system-level challenge requiring co-design across physics, materials, architecture, and software.
Advanced packaging, photonics, and AI-driven design are converging, making it increasingly difficult to optimize these technologies in isolation.
The industry is undergoing a fundamental shift toward 're-engineering engineering,' where the workload itself defines the optimization parameters for the entire hardware stack.

posts.title: CATL expands battery swap partnership as BAIC plans adoption across multiple brands
posts.summary:
BAIC will connect models across multiple brands to CATL's battery swap network and open its dealer network to support station construction.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BAIC Group and CATL have deepened their partnership to integrate multiple BAIC brands into the Choco-SEB battery swap network.
The collaboration includes opening BAIC's dealer network to facilitate the construction of public energy replenishment infrastructure.
The companies aim to establish a mature battery swap ecosystem capable of serving a million-level vehicle population, leveraging recurring revenue models from battery rentals.
